definition: A memory-efficient pre-training method that projects gradients into a low-rank subspace, allowing full-parameter training with far less optimizer memory.
details: GaLore exploits the low-rank structure of gradients to compute optimizer states in a reduced subspace, cutting memory usage for training LLMs on consumer GPUs. It does not alter the model architecture and can be combined with 8-bit optimizers. The approach approaches full-rank pre-training quality on benchmarks while reducing memory substantially.

explainer.lead: GaLore is a memory-saving training method that keeps optimizer statistics for a compressed, low-rank version of the gradients. It matters because it lets all of a model's weights be trained, not just adapters, on much smaller GPUs.

tiers.eli5: Imagine taking notes on a long lecture by writing down only the few main themes instead of every word. GaLore stores a short summary of how the model wants to change, which takes far less room but still guides learning well.
tiers.practitioner: Each weight's gradient is projected onto a few top singular directions, the Adam states are kept in that small space, and the update is projected back to full size; the projection is refreshed every few hundred steps. It can be combined with 8-bit optimizers, and the rank and refresh interval trade memory against quality.
tiers.paperLevel: Zhao et al. argue that gradients of matrix-shaped weights become low-rank during training, so optimizer states can live in a subspace obtained from periodic SVD of the gradient. Unlike LoRA, the weights themselves stay full-rank, and switching subspaces over time lets training cover the full parameter space with far less optimizer memory.

explainer.example: Pre-training a 7B model on a single 24 GB consumer GPU becomes possible by combining GaLore with an 8-bit optimizer.

citation.title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
